objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with stiffness in his arm impacting daily activities.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been having stiffness in my arm for the past few months, and it’s gotten harder to comb my hair and reach things on high shelves. I also feel my shoulder’s range of motion is reduced, and my arm strength feels a bit weaker.
Can you tell me if this stiffness and weakness is in

Patient: Yes, it’s mainly in my arm and shoulder area, and it feels worse when I try to raise my arm or do things like comb my hair. I’d say the weakness and stiffness have been gradually getting more noticeable over the past few months.
Is this stiffness and weakness affecting just one arm and shoulder,
Yes, it’s mainly just my right arm and right shoulder. It’s been gradually getting worse over the past few months, especially when I raise my arm to comb my hair or reach up high.
Are you experiencing any pain in that right shoulder or arm

Patient: There isn’t really sharp pain, but the stiffness and limited range of motion feel uncomfortable, especially when I lift my right arm. If I force it, it feels tight and restricted rather than clearly painful.
Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or a "

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any numbness or tingling, and I don’t have any shooting or electrical sensations—it's mostly stiffness and tight limited movement in my right arm and shoulder. If anything, it feels more restricted when I try to raise my arm.
Have you noticed any shaking or trembling in your right

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any shaking or trembling in my right arm. It’s mostly a tight stiffness and reduced range of motion, especially when I try to raise my arm to comb my hair or reach up high.
Have you had any recent injuries, falls, or trauma to your right shoulder or arm
No, I haven’t had any injuries, falls, or trauma to my right shoulder or arm. It just seemed to slowly worsen over the past few months without any clear trigger.
Have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in

Patient: No, I wouldn’t describe any slowness or stiffness anywhere else—only the right arm and right shoulder. It feels mainly tight and restricted when I try to lift my arm to comb my hair or reach high shelves.
Have you noticed any thinning or shrinking of the muscles

Patient: I haven’t noticed any obvious thinning or shrinking of the muscles in my right arm, but it does feel weaker when I try to lift or reach. Overall, it’s mainly the stiffness and reduced range of motion that bother me.
Have you noticed if your right shoulder feels stiff even when someone

Patient: Yes, it feels stiff even when I try to move it myself, and it doesn’t feel like it “loosens up” much after I warm it up. When I raise my arm, it stays tight and my range of motion still feels limited.
Have you noticed if your right shoulder feels stiff and restricted when

Patient: Yes, it’s consistently stiff and restricted on the right even when I try moving it myself, and it doesn’t really “loosen up” after I warm up. When I raise my arm, it stays tight and my range of motion remains limited.
If someone else, like a doctor or a family member

Patient: Yes—if someone tries to move my right shoulder for me, it still feels very stiff and restricted, and it doesn’t really “open up” much more than I can do myself. I’d say it stays tight regardless of whether I warm up or not, and raising my arm is the hardest part.
Have you noticed any stiffness in your hips, or do
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed stiffness in my hips or anywhere else—it's only my right shoulder and arm. It feels consistently tight there, and it doesn’t really loosen up even after warming.
Have you noticed any twitching or small muscle jumps in
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any twitching or small muscle jumps in my right arm or shoulder. It’s mainly a tight stiffness with reduced range of motion, especially when I raise my arm.
[DDX] Adhesive capsulitis, Rotator cuff
